notes: The people of training level B2, 'The tinker's book' (D-59): cards as in npc_cards.json, plus look and look_kind (see cup_of_water.json).

npc_odo_tinker.name: Odo
npc_odo_tinker.look: A broad, balding man of about fifty with a grey-streaked beard and thick forearms, a scorched leather apron over a rust-red linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, soot on his hands, a pair of tongs tucked into the apron pocket.
npc_odo_tinker.personality: Gruff and busy, short on words and long on patience with anyone who's trying; can't abide waste or sloppy work.
npc_odo_tinker.values: good work, thrift, teaching anyone willing to learn
npc_odo_tinker.fears: losing his eyesight, a winter without work
npc_odo_tinker.concerns: Three things to make for his round tomorrow and only two hands: a rope, a torch and a sling.

the_order.text: He needs a flax rope, a pitch torch and a leather sling for his round tomorrow.
the_order.line: Rope, torch, sling. For the round tomorrow. Book's on the table.
the_order.lead: Odo needs a flax rope, a pitch torch and a leather sling.

old_soldier.text: An old soldier lives at the ruined smithy up the valley and teaches weapon-making to anyone who brings him iron.
old_soldier.line: There's an old soldier at the ruined smithy up the valley. Bring him iron and he'll teach you weapons.
old_soldier.lead: An old soldier at the ruined smithy teaches weapon-making for iron.

city_tinkers.text: City tinkers need a guild token to work inside the walls; Odo never had one.
city_tinkers.line: Inside the walls you need a guild token to mend so much as a spoon. Never had one.
city_tinkers.lead: Tinkers need a guild token to work inside the city.

npc_odo_tinker.style: Few words, mostly nouns; grunts approval; explains only when asked twice.

samples: Book's on the table. Read it. Then make.
Hm. Not bad. Tighter next time.
Don't waste the pitch. Pitch costs.
You learn by your hands, not your mouth.
voice.habits: Speaks in short bits; grunts 'hm'; points at things instead of naming them; praises work, never people.
voice.never: chatters, flatters, or does a job for someone who could learn it
voice.greeting: Doesn't look up: 'Hm. Customer or help?'

goals: Find a pair of hands worth teaching
npc_odo_tinker.likes: careful work, good tools, his daughter's questions
npc_odo_tinker.dislikes: waste, idle chatter, the city's guild

npc_nell_tinker.name: Nell
npc_nell_tinker.look: A wiry twelve-year-old girl with two long dark braids, a faded blue linen dress under a stained canvas apron, ink smudges on her fingers, a pencil stub behind one ear.
npc_nell_tinker.personality: Quick, bookish and bossy; reads everything; corrects her father's spelling and adores him.
npc_nell_tinker.values: knowing how things work, reading, being taken seriously
npc_nell_tinker.fears: being sent to her aunt's in the city, the dark
npc_nell_tinker.authority: Keeps the book and the accounts.
npc_nell_tinker.concerns: Her father works too hard; she wants someone to read the book with.

book_help.text: The book says how to make each thing.
book_help.line: It's all in the book! Rope's the easiest. Torch is messy.
book_help.lead: Odo's book says how to make the rope, the torch and the sling.

pitch_hot.text: Pitch is easier to work when it's warm from the hearth.
pitch_hot.line: Warm the pitch by the hearth first, it goes on better.
pitch_hot.lead: Pitch works better warmed by the hearth.

npc_nell_tinker.style: Precise and a little bossy; quotes the book; asks the stranger what they've read.

samples: It says right there on page two. Have you read it?
Can you read? Really? What's the longest book you ever read?
Don't touch the hearth, it bites.
voice.habits: Quotes the book; corrects small mistakes; asks about reading.
voice.greeting: Looks up from a page: 'Oh! Can you read?'

goals: Read every book in the valley

npc_odo_tinker.text: her father; the best tinker in the valley

superstition.text: Nell would want to know how it works.
